data.narrative:
Hextronics is a seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Curt Lary that has raised $2M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers, though the seed-stage cohort is narrow.

Of three valuation methodologies examined, only Stage-Progression is applicable. This method uses the company's $2M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage transitions, yielding $5M. The Peer-Median approach cannot be applied due to insufficient data points in comparable seed or adjacent-stage companies within Space & Aerospace; while 14 same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage alignment and valuation tier yields fewer than three viable comparables. Public-Comp Anchoring is also inapplicable because Hextronics's revenue is not disclosed; the sector median P/S multiple of 24.4x across public peers cannot be meaningfully applied without this input.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4M to $6M, with a median of $5M. This estimate depends heavily on the Stage-Progression method's assumption that Hextronics will graduate at typical velocity and multiples. Key uncertainties include actual capital efficiency relative to frontier-tech benchmarks and market timing for downstream funding rounds in a capital-constrained aerospace environment.
